# parametricboot

parametricboot automates the **parametric bootstrap** for fitted
regression models. You fit a model as usual; the package simulates new
responses from it, refits the model to each of them, and turns the
replicates into bias estimates, standard errors, confidence intervals,
prediction intervals, likelihood-ratio tests and diagnostic plots.

Supported models:

| Model | Fitted with | How replicates are generated |
|----|----|----|
| Linear and generalised linear models | [`lm()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html), [`glm()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/glm.html) | [`simulate()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/simulate.html), then the original call is re-evaluated |
| Negative-binomial regression | [`MASS::glm.nb()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/MASS/man/glm.nb.html) | `MASS::simulate.negbin()` with fitted theta; re-estimate theta on each refit |
| Linear and generalised linear mixed models | [`lme4::lmer()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/lme4/man/lmer.html), [`lme4::glmer()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/lme4/man/glmer.html) | [`simulate()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/simulate.html), then [`lme4::refit()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/lme4/man/refit.html) |
| Cox proportional hazards models | [`survival::coxph()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/survival/man/coxph.html) | model-based resampling (Davison & Hinkley, 1997, Algorithm 7.3) |

## Validated model classes

The base-R [`lm()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/lm.html) and
[`glm()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/glm.html) classes use the validated
linear-model/GLM bootstrap engine. Inheriting from `lm` or `glm` is not,
by itself, a guarantee that simulating and refitting preserves a model’s
assumptions: unvalidated subclasses such as
[`mgcv::gam()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/mgcv/man/gam.html) and
[`stats::aov()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/aov.html) fail explicitly
rather than returning unverified bootstrap results. The exact
[`MASS::glm.nb()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/MASS/man/glm.nb.html) class is
now separately supported: response simulation uses the fitted
negative-binomial mean and dispersion, and refitting re-estimates
dispersion in each replicate. Non-unit prior weights remain unsupported
because `simulate.negbin()` ignores them. Quasi-likelihood families are
also rejected because they lack a fully specified parametric sampling
law.

The supported `lme4` mixed models and right-censored `coxph` workflows
are unaffected. Additional model classes will be admitted after separate
mathematical and computational validation.

## Installation

parametricboot is a work in progress: it is not on CRAN, and the
interface may still change. Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("DiogoRibeiro7/parametricboot")
```

## Predicting new observations

The existing
[`pb_predict_boot()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_predict_boot.md)
describes uncertainty in conditional mean predictions. Prediction
intervals for an *individual future observation* must also account for
response noise. Use
[`pb_predict_interval()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_predict_interval.md)
to simulate a new outcome from each refitted sampling distribution:

``` r

fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
boot <- pb_simulate(fit, n = 300, seed = 42, keep_fits = TRUE)
new_cars <- mtcars[1:3, c("wt", "hp")]
pb_predict_interval(boot, new_cars, level = 0.95, seed = 17)
```

For further analysis,
[`pb_predict_observations()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_predict_observations.md)
returns the individual simulated outcomes. This first version supports
unweighted Gaussian linear, Poisson and negative-binomial regression
models; it does not yet support binomial, Cox or mixed models. These are
approximate model-conditional predictive intervals, not guaranteed exact
frequentist intervals.

## Memory-efficient bootstrap predictions

Supply `newdata` when bootstrapping to store one numeric prediction per
row per successful refit, without keeping refitted model objects. Use
`predict_args` to set prediction options explicitly. The cached request
is checked so that a later call cannot silently return predictions for
different inputs.

``` r

fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
new_cars <- mtcars[1:3, c("wt", "hp")]
boot <- pb_simulate(fit, n = 100, seed = 2, keep_fits = FALSE,
                    newdata = new_cars)
quantiles <- t(apply(pb_predict_boot(boot), 1, stats::quantile,
                     probs = c(0.025, 0.975)))
```

This caches conditional mean predictions rather than predictive
intervals for a new observation; the latter also require response noise.

## Derived statistics

You can bootstrap a named statistic of any supported fitted model, such
as an odds ratio, slope contrast or threshold. The same summaries and
non-studentised intervals apply. The default coefficient workflow is
unchanged.

``` r

model <- glm(vs ~ mpg, data = mtcars, family = binomial())
boot <- pb_simulate(model, n = 200, seed = 1, keep_fits = FALSE,
                    statistic = function(fit) c(odds_ratio = exp(coef(fit)[[2L]])))
pb_confint(boot, type = "percentile")
pb_mc_error(boot)
```

Studentised intervals for a derived statistic are available when a
`statistic_se(fit)` callback provides a matching, strictly positive,
model-justified standard error on every refit. For example, the delta
method supplies the standard error of a GLM odds ratio:

``` r

s <- function(fit) c(odds_ratio = unname(exp(coef(fit)[[2L]])))
s_se <- function(fit) {
  beta <- unname(coef(fit)[[2L]])
  c(odds_ratio = exp(beta) * sqrt(unname(vcov(fit)[2, 2])))
}
boot <- pb_simulate(model, n = 200, seed = 1, keep_fits = FALSE,
                    statistic = s, statistic_se = s_se)
pb_confint(boot, type = "student")
```

Without that callback, studentised derived-statistic intervals remain
unavailable. The package checks callback structure and positivity, not
the mathematical correctness of a supplied standard error.

## Goodness-of-fit checks

[`pb_gof()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_gof.md)
compares a deviance, Pearson statistic or count of zeros with the
simulated, refitted reference distribution of a supported binomial or
count regression model. The default `tail = "greater"` identifies
unusually large discrepancies or excess zeros; `tail = "less"` tests for
unusually few zeros or small discrepancy values.

``` r

counts <- data.frame(y = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 0, 1, 1, 2))
model <- glm(y ~ 1, data = counts, family = poisson())
check <- pb_gof(model, n = 200, statistic = "zeros",
                tail = "less", seed = 1)
pb_gof_mc_error(check)
pb_plot_gof(check)
```

The Monte Carlo limits describe simulation uncertainty in the tail
probability, conditional on the fitted model and successful refits; they
do not establish whether the model is correctly specified.

## Monte Carlo precision of bootstrap summaries

The functions
[`pb_mc_error()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_mc_error.md)
and
[`pb_confint_mc_error()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_confint_mc_error.md)
quantify how much a finite number of successful bootstrap replicates
affects the estimated bias, bootstrap standard error and the limits of
percentile, basic or studentised confidence intervals. Interval limit
diagnostics use conservative binomial order-statistic ranks; they may be
unbounded when the number of simulations is too small. These are
per-endpoint Monte Carlo bounds, not confidence intervals for the
unknown model parameter. For normal-approximation intervals, Monte Carlo
precision uses a joint delta method retaining covariance between the
simulated mean and standard deviation; those bounds are approximate.

``` r

model <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
sim <- pb_simulate(model, n = 100, seed = 42, keep_fits = FALSE)
pb_mc_error(sim)
pb_confint_mc_error(sim, level = 0.8, mc_level = 0.9)
```

## Monte Carlo precision for bootstrap tests

A bootstrap p-value depends on how many successful refits were
simulated.
[`pb_lrt_mc_error()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_lrt_mc_error.md)
reports its binomial Monte Carlo standard error and an exact interval
for the bootstrap exceedance probability. It retains the add-one
corrected p-value reported by
[`pb_lrt()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_lrt.md);
the interval refers to simulation variability, not model uncertainty.
Failed refits are counted and excluded, so selective refit failure
remains a potential source of bias.

``` r

null <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
alternative <- update(null, . ~ . + hp)
test <- pb_lrt(null, alternative, n = 199, seed = 1)
pb_lrt_mc_error(test)
```

## Structured input validation

Shared argument checks for bootstrap counts, seeds, confidence levels,
bootstrap results and parameter selection now raise native R
`dataexcept` conditions. They retain their existing error messages, gain
a `parametricboot_validation_error` class, and classify invalid
unchanged inputs as permanently non-retryable. This does not change the
simulation algorithms, statistical results, or how refit failures and
warnings are handled.

``` r

fit <- stats::lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
error <- tryCatch(pb_simulate(fit, n = 0), error = identity)
inherits(error, "parametricboot_validation_error") # TRUE
dataexcept::is_retryable(error)                  # FALSE
```

Until `dataexcept` is published to a package repository, the development
installation resolves its exact pinned GitHub revision via
`DESCRIPTION`.

## Example

A classic dose-response experiment (Collett, 1991): batches of 20
tobacco budworm moths of each sex were exposed to six doses of a
pyrethroid, and the number killed was recorded. That is only 12 binomial
observations, so how far can the large-sample theory behind
`summary(fit)` be trusted?

``` r

library(parametricboot)

budworm <- data.frame(
  sex = rep(c("M", "F"), each = 6),
  dose = rep(c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32), times = 2),
  dead = c(1, 4, 9, 13, 18, 20, 0, 2, 6, 10, 12, 16),
  n = 20
)
fit <- glm(cbind(dead, n - dead) ~ sex + log2(dose), data = budworm, family = binomial())

res <- pb_simulate(fit, n = 1000, seed = 2025)
res
#> <pb_boot> Parametric bootstrap
#>   Model:      glm (binomial)
#>   Replicates: 1000
#>   Terms:      (Intercept), sexM, log2(dose)
```

[`pb_summary_table()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_summary_table.md)
reports, for each coefficient, the bootstrap estimates of bias, standard
error and mean squared error, the actual coverage of the nominal 95%
Wald interval, and a bootstrap confidence interval:

``` r

pb_summary_table(res)
#>          term  estimate boot_mean        bias std_error        mse coverage
#> 1 (Intercept) -3.473155 -3.552493 -0.07933778 0.4839494 0.24026729    0.954
#> 2        sexM  1.100743  1.117377  0.01663401 0.3784177 0.14333343    0.945
#> 3  log2(dose)  1.064214  1.088388  0.02417447 0.1352250 0.01885192    0.946
#>        lower     upper
#> 1 -4.5809602 -2.702189
#> 2  0.4015961  1.856280
#> 3  0.8444751  1.401441
```

Here the news is good: the slope is overestimated by about 2%, a small
fraction of its standard error, and the Wald intervals cover as
advertised. The bootstrap distributions are close to normal:

``` r

pb_plot_estimates(res)
```

![Histograms of 1000 bootstrap estimates of the intercept, the sex
effect and the log-dose slope. Each is roughly symmetric and centred
near the original estimate, which is marked by a dashed
line.](reference/figures/README-estimates-1.png)

The same replicates give intervals for any prediction, here the
dose-response curve for male moths:

``` r

males <- data.frame(sex = "M", dose = seq(1, 32, length.out = 100))
pb_plot_predictions(res, males, x = "dose", type = "response")
```

![Predicted probability of death for male moths rising from about 0.1 at
dose 1 to 0.95 at dose 32, with a shaded 95 percent bootstrap band that
is widest at low doses.](reference/figures/README-predictions-1.png)

## Functions

| Task | Functions |
|----|----|
| Draw replicates | [`pb_simulate()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_simulate.md), [`pb_parallel()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_parallel.md), [`pb_drop_warned()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_drop_warned.md) |
| Summarise | [`pb_summary_table()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_summary_table.md), [`pb_key_stats()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_key_stats.md), [`pb_confint()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_confint.md), [`pb_tidy()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_tidy.md), plus [`print()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/print.html), [`summary()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/summary.html) and [`confint()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/confint.html) methods |
| Visualise | [`pb_plot_estimates()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_plot_estimates.md), [`pb_plot_diagnostics()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_plot_diagnostics.md), [`pb_plot_predictions()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_plot_predictions.md) |
| Predict | [`pb_predict_boot()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_predict_boot.md) |
| Test nested models | [`pb_lrt()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_lrt.md), [`pb_plot_lrt()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_plot_lrt.md) |
| Compare other models | [`pb_compare_models()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_compare_models.md) |
| Nonparametric helper | [`pb_resample()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_resample.md) |

The [getting-started
article](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/articles/parametricboot.html)
([`vignette("parametricboot")`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/articles/parametricboot.md))
is a tour that also covers mixed models, Cox models, bootstrap
likelihood-ratio tests, and what to do when some refits misbehave. The
full [function
reference](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/) is
on the package website.

Please report bugs and request features on the [issue
tracker](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/parametricboot/issues).
Contributions are welcome; see the [contributing
guide](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/CONTRIBUTING.md).
This project follows a [code of
conduct](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

# Package index

## Draw bootstrap replicates

- [`pb_simulate()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_simulate.md)
  : Run parametric bootstrap replicates
- [`pb_parallel()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_parallel.md)
  : Run parametric bootstrap replicates in parallel
- [`pb_drop_warned()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_drop_warned.md)
  : Drop replicates whose refit raised a warning

## Summarise

- [`pb_summary_table()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_summary_table.md)
  : Summarise bootstrap statistics and confidence intervals

- [`pb_key_stats()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_key_stats.md)
  : Bootstrap bias, standard error, MSE and coverage

- [`pb_confint()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_confint.md)
  : Bootstrap confidence intervals

- [`pb_mc_error()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_mc_error.md)
  : Monte Carlo errors of bootstrap bias and standard error

- [`pb_confint_mc_error()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_confint_mc_error.md)
  : Monte Carlo precision of bootstrap confidence interval limits

- [`pb_tidy()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_tidy.md)
  : Convert bootstrap estimates to long format

- [`print(`*`<pb_boot>`*`)`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_boot-methods.md)
  [`summary(`*`<pb_boot>`*`)`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_boot-methods.md)
  [`confint(`*`<pb_boot>`*`)`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_boot-methods.md)
  :

  Methods for `pb_boot` objects

## Visualise

- [`pb_plot_estimates()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_plot_estimates.md)
  : Plot the bootstrap distribution of the estimates
- [`pb_plot_diagnostics()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_plot_diagnostics.md)
  : Plot bootstrap diagnostics
- [`pb_plot_predictions()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_plot_predictions.md)
  : Plot predictions with bootstrap intervals

## Test and compare models

- [`pb_gof()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_gof.md)
  : Parametric-bootstrap goodness-of-fit test
- [`pb_gof_mc_error()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_gof_mc_error.md)
  : Monte Carlo uncertainty of a bootstrap goodness-of-fit p-value
- [`pb_plot_gof()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_plot_gof.md)
  : Plot a simulated goodness-of-fit reference distribution
- [`pb_lrt()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_lrt.md)
  [`print(`*`<pb_lrt>`*`)`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_lrt.md)
  : Parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test for nested models
- [`pb_lrt_mc_error()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_lrt_mc_error.md)
  : Monte Carlo uncertainty for a parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio
  p-value
- [`pb_plot_lrt()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_plot_lrt.md)
  : Plot the bootstrap null distribution of a likelihood-ratio statistic
- [`pb_compare_models()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_compare_models.md)
  : Compare models by the bootstrap distribution of a fit metric

## Predict

- [`pb_predict_boot()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_predict_boot.md)
  : Predict with bootstrap uncertainty
- [`pb_predict_interval()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_predict_interval.md)
  : Prediction intervals for new observations
- [`pb_predict_observations()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_predict_observations.md)
  : Simulate future observations from parametric bootstrap refits
- [`pb_predict_variance()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_predict_variance.md)
  : Decompose model-conditional predictive variance

## Helpers

- [`pb_resample()`](https://diogoribeiro7.github.io/parametricboot/reference/pb_resample.md)
  : Resample the rows of a data frame with replacement
